cards.heading: Definition: three testing layers
cards.question: What are the three architectural layers that layered testing of agentic systems scopes each test to?
cards.answer: A deterministic system shell (APIs, integrations, tool implementations), an orchestration layer that assembles the runtime prompt (deterministic given its inputs), and a black-box inference core reachable only through prompt and state.

cards.heading: Why layering works: most of the app is deterministic
cards.question: What insight does the layering exploit to make testing a nondeterministic agentic system tractable?
cards.answer: Most of an agentic application is not actually nondeterministic — splitting the stack localizes the nondeterminism to one layer, the inference core, and lets conventional testing keep working everywhere else.

cards.heading: Orchestration bugs are never model faults
cards.question: Why can a wrong prompt (unresolved placeholder, stale state, truncated history) be caught deterministically and never blamed on the model?
cards.answer: Because prompt construction is a pure function of template, state, and user input at the orchestration layer, so a wrong prompt is a deterministic bug in that function, not a model failure.

cards.heading: Inference core: relational, not exact assertions
cards.question: What kinds of assertions replace exact-value checks at the black-box inference core?
cards.answer: Metamorphic tests (a defined input change should produce a defined output change), property tests (invariants across generated inputs), and behavioural harnesses (mock APIs and injected failures observing task-completion order and tool-selection consistency).

cards.heading: Adversarial checks are resilience, not correctness
cards.question: How are adversarial suites — prompt-injection resistance, tool-failure handling — scoped within this framework?
cards.answer: As resilience testing, not correctness testing — they probe whether the system degrades safely under attack or failure, not whether its output is the 'right' one.
